title: Canonical inverse- and direct-image coefficient comparisons
statement: Let Λ and Λ′ be commutative rings in Type(u+1), φ:Λ→Λ′ a ring homomorphism, and f:Z→W a scheme morphism. The sectionwise identity f_* Res_φ = Res_φ f_* gives a canonical bounded-below derived comparison Rf_* Res_φ ≅ Res_φ Rf_*. Inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] similarly commutes with Res_φ, canonically by uniqueness of left adjoints to the sectionwise direct-image/coextension composite. Applying the exact derived functor gives D⁺Res_φ D⁺f^* ≅ D⁺f^* D⁺Res_φ. The source and target coefficient isomorphisms for the two composites in [sbc-def-base-change-map] are constructed by composing these isomorphisms. In particular, the canonical direct-image comparison morphism is invertible.

source.document: Stacks Project, Cohomology on Sites, and Mathlib

proof.text: Direct image is precomposition and restriction is coefficient postcomposition, so their comparison is Iso.refl. The two inverse-image/restriction composites are left adjoints to the same composite of direct image and coextension, hence leftAdjointUniq constructs their natural isomorphism.

Lift the inverse-image isomorphism using mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso and the exact-functor composition isomorphisms. Define the direct-image map with rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange on the sectionwise identity.
Apply isIso_rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange_of_rightAcyclic to the restricted-injective acyclicity theorem. Turn this canonical map into an isomorphism with asIso.

Whisker the inverse of the direct-image comparison with derived inverse image for the source, then compose with the inverse-image comparison. For the target, first whisker the inverse-image comparison with derived direct image and then compose with the inverse of the direct-image comparison.
